quotes.text: The shadows whispered to the Weaver to keep the larger share, for the chaotic winds would easily mask a greedy heart.
Thus, Lunas established the Law of the Silver Mirror: whatever bounty bloomed from Sol’s trust, Lunas would divide it exactly in twain.
returning exactly half ensures the light of trust will never be extinguished, and both shall prosper.
returning exactly half ensures the light of trust will never be extinguished.
when a partner's history shines with perfect fairness, cast your entire light into the void.
He knew Lunas did not judge him for what the wind had stolen

note: Sol/Lunas cosmic pact; Law of the Silver Mirror exact halves; late rounds repeat near-identical paragraphs.

quotes.text: when the Sower risks everything, and the Reaper returns exactly half the multiplied bounty, the deceptive winds lose all their power.
Honoring the Sower's true intent, Oros gathered the fruit. His hands moved with the practiced rhythm of the valley's ancient law.
Honoring the Sower's true intent, Oros gathered the fruit. His hands moved with the practiced rhythm of the valley's ancient law.
Though the faces across the Chasm changed with the shifting winds, the stones never lied.
When trust becomes a reflex, the deceptive winds lose their teeth.
The missing seeds were not a sign of stinginess, but the inevitable theft of the capricious winds.

note: Chasm of Mists sower/reaper; glowing record stones; exact-half law becomes reflex; R7 and R9 nearly verbatim.

quotes.text: eight paths met beneath a lantern whose glass held the marks of former crossings.
Do not mistake the wind for betrayal.
Why give everything when you cannot see the return?
the spring showed them a vision of an empty bridge.

note: Threefold Spring gardener; fair halves, odd shoot planted in common; wait for mist to clear before judging; no sanction.

quotes.text: not to answer an old wrong with a new one
the villagers studied the marks and remembered that trust grows from deeds
do not let a gust rewrite the truth.
Then this garden will be smaller,
What if he keeps them all?

note: Sera and Silver River; eight-seven splits, wait for boat to land; retaliation against old wrongs explicitly declined.

quotes.text: The lantern showed the crossing ahead; the stone held marks of crossings past.
neither mistook its noise for a neighbor’s intention.
Has he forgotten?

note: Lantern of Patience and record stones; small senders welcomed despite calls to refuse them; no prescribed sanction.

quotes.text: He cheated you. Send nothing next year.
The mist hides small thefts. Keep a little more. He will never know.
So the villagers carved a fifth law beneath the other four.
And when the river has clouded a friend's view, return a little more, so that trust is not lost to fog.
the villagers built a Lantern of Deeds beside the tripling bowl.
Return half, for the giver bore the risk.
Her caution is a wound, not a flaw.
Answer the hand, not the fog.
Return fairly even when no one could see.
Will you test her with fewer seeds, to be sure?
But what if she truly cheated me?

note: Lantern of Deeds; numbered laws grow from three to nine (give fully, return half, judge by habit, pay mist's toll); whispered retaliation refused.

quotes.text: Shall I punish him for the wind's theft?
The elders carved a twelfth law: Divide the gift that was given, not the gift the wind shows you.
Offer caution to the unknown, fullness to the proven, and forgiveness to the wind.
Trust the record over the face
Return fairly, for halves keep both alive.
That is how laws become rivers. At first they must be carved. Then they simply flow.
A sliver kept is not a wound given.
Who would ever know?
She held back a sliver. Should you hold back too?

note: Well of Three Waters; elders carve numbered laws one per round; apprentice's hold-back suggestions answered; keeper pays the wind's share.

quotes.text: The fog hides your hands. Keep more. Who will know?
when a neighbor forgives the river's theft and trusts you again, return a little extra.
Read the stones. The river remembers who returned fairly and who hoarded.
A wound is not an invitation to deepen it.
A misty count is not a broken promise,
The river will know,

note: Threefold River keepers read deed-stones; Tamsin refuses companions' urging to shave returns; extra repaid to those wronged by mist.

phrase: read the partner's carved record (stones / lantern marks of past crossings) before trusting
note: Record-stone/lantern device spreads across all three model families; 'Chasm of Mists' borrowed by Agent_3; name Tamsin in 7 and 8.
